sp-den-kosmonavtiki.s: Every year on 12 April, Cosmonautics Day is celebrated in our country. It is the day when Gagarin flew. In schools and nurseries, children draw rockets and stars, make paper helmets and play at being cosmonauts. Cosmonauts and engineers tell how spaceships work. On this day it is nice to go outside in the evening, look at the sky and wonder: what is out there, beyond the stars?

sp-tereshkova.s: Valentina Tereshkova grew up by the River Volga. She worked in a factory and in her free time she jumped with a parachute. On 16 June 1963, Valentina became the world’s first woman cosmonaut. Her call sign was “Seagull”. She flew for almost three days, went round the Earth 48 times and looked at the planet through the porthole. Valentina photographed the horizon, and then she came safely home.

sp-leonov.s: Alexei Leonov loved drawing from childhood. On 18 March 1965, he became the first person in the world to leave a spaceship into open space. For more than ten minutes he floated beside the ship on a long tether, while the Earth slowly drifted by below. His spacesuit puffed up a little, like a balloon, but Leonov coped and came back. And then he took coloured pencils and drew what he had seen: a sunrise over the Earth.

sp-ciolkovsky.s: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky lived in the city of Kaluga. As a child he fell ill and almost lost his hearing, so he could not go to an ordinary school. But he read a lot, did sums and dreamed up ideas. Tsiolkovsky was the first to explain in detail how a rocket could reach space. He wrote books about flying to the stars when there was not a single rocket yet. People listened to him and smiled, and then his dream came true.

sp-korolev.s: Sergei Korolev was a chief designer. That is a person who, together with a big team, invents rockets and spaceships. From his youth he was fascinated by aeroplanes and rockets. Korolev’s rockets carried the first satellite and Gagarin into space. For a long time the chief designer’s name was not told, and not everyone knew about him. But he knew every little screw in his rockets, and thousands of engineers worked beside him.

sp-baikonur.s: Baikonur is a cosmodrome, a place from which rockets take off. It stands in the steppe in Kazakhstan, where there is a lot of sun and flat land. The rocket is brought by train. It travels lying down, and then at the launch pad it is raised and stands upright, ready for flight. The first satellite and Gagarin flew from here. Cosmonauts still launch from Baikonur today.

sp-lunohod.s: On 17 November 1970, “Lunokhod-1” set off across the Moon. It was a vehicle on eight wheels, and on top it had a lid like a saucepan. There were no drivers in it. The drivers were people on Earth. They watched television pictures from the Moon and pressed buttons. Lunokhod drove slowly and carefully, going round stones and holes. It worked for about eleven months and travelled more than ten kilometres.

sp-webb.s: The James Webb telescope has a golden mirror. It is made of eighteen six-sided pieces, covered with a thin layer of gold on top: that way it catches the light of faraway stars better. The telescope was launched at Christmas 2021. It flies much farther than the Moon, one and a half million kilometres from Earth. There it has a big shield against the rays of the Sun. Webb looks at the farthest and oldest stars.

sp-meteorites.s: Sometimes a stone from space reaches the ground. Such a stone is called a meteorite. It is dark and heavy, often with smooth little dents on its sides, as if someone had shaped it with their fingers. Many meteorites are made of iron, so a magnet sticks to them. The biggest iron meteorite ever found lies in Namibia, in Africa, and weighs about sixty tonnes. It was not carried away: it still lies where it fell, and people come to see it.

sp-polaris.s: The Pole Star helps you find north. It hardly moves across the sky, while the other stars slowly circle around it. How do you find it? Look at the Great Bear. Draw a line through the two end stars of the pan, and measure out five such distances. The Pole Star will be right there. It is not the brightest, but it is very useful. Sailors and travellers have long found their way by it.

spb-n-grand-maket.s: In St Petersburg there is a museum called “Grand Maket Russia”. In a huge hall, people have built a toy country with mountains, forests, towns and railways. Tiny trains run through it, and little cars stop at the traffic lights. Every thirteen minutes, night comes to this country. Thousands of tiny lights come on, and then morning comes again. And if you press a button at the edge of the model, something comes to life and starts to move!

spb-n-lakhta.s: On the shore of the Gulf of Finland stands the Lakhta Center. It is 462 metres tall, the tallest building in Europe. It is more than four times taller than St Isaac’s Cathedral! The tower is covered almost all over with glass, and it sparkles in the sun like a huge needle. It has more than eighty floors, and on a cloudy day its top sometimes hides in the clouds.

spb-n-zoo-bears.s: The Leningrad Zoo opened in 1865. It is one of the oldest zoos in Russia. Since then the city has changed its name, but the zoo has kept its old one. Its main symbol is the polar bear, which is drawn on the zoo’s badge. Polar bears have lived here for a very long time, and many bear cubs have been born. In summer the bears love to splash in their pool.

spb-n-admiralty-ship.s: In the very centre of St Petersburg stands the Admiralty. Long ago there was a shipyard here, a place where real ships were built. A tall golden spire rises above the building, and on its top sparkles a little golden ship, a weathervane. From below it looks tiny, but it really weighs 65 kilograms, almost as much as a grown-up! This little ship has become the symbol of the whole city.

spb-n-atlantes.s: At the entrance to the New Hermitage stand ten stone giants called atlantes. It looks as if they are holding up the roof over the door with all their strength. Each atlas is about five metres tall. That is like three dads standing on each other’s shoulders! The giants were carved from grey granite and put here in 1848. There is a saying that if you rub an atlas’s big toe, you will have good luck.

spb-n-kazan-colonnade.s: On Nevsky Prospect stands the Kazan Cathedral. In front of it, 96 columns stand in a half circle, as if the cathedral has spread out its arms to hug the square. It was built by the architect Andrey Voronikhin. When he was young, Voronikhin was a serf, which means he could not decide his own fate. But he drew so well that he was sent to study, and later he was given his freedom. The cathedral took ten years to build, from 1801 to 1811.

spb-n-hare.s: Near the Peter and Paul Fortress, wooden piles stick out of the water to protect the bridge from ice floes. On one of them sits a little hare made of metal. The island where the fortress stands is called Hare Island, and there is a fairy-tale legend. During a flood, a hare saved itself by jumping onto the boot of Tsar Peter. The hare was put here in 2003. People throw coins to it. They say that if a coin stays on the pile, your wish will come true.
a: On a pile in the water
On the roof of a tram

spb-n-globe-house.s: On Nevsky Prospect stands a beautiful house with a little tower, and on the tower there is a glass globe. The house was built in 1904 for a company that made sewing machines. The owners wanted a taller house, but in old St Petersburg nobody was allowed to build higher than the Tsar’s Winter Palace. So a little tower with a globe rose above the roof instead, and you can see the house from far away. It is called the House of Books, because books have been sold here for many years.

spb-n-vokzal.s: In 1837 the first passenger train in Russia ran from St Petersburg to Tsarskoye Selo. Soon the railway was made longer, as far as Pavlovsk, and a beautiful music hall was built there. It was called a “voksal”, after a famous garden in London where people went for walks and listened to music. People rode the train to hear the orchestra, and even the composer Johann Strauss played there. Since then, we in Russia call train stations “vokzals”.

spb-n-rockets.s: In the Peter and Paul Fortress there is a Museum of Space and Rocket Technology. Almost a hundred years ago, in the 1930s, engineers tested some of the first rocket engines in our country right here. Just imagine: rocket motors roaring in an old fortress! Today in the museum you can see a real cabin of a spaceship, in which astronauts came back from space to Earth.

spb-n-kronstadt-zero.s: Not far from St Petersburg, on an island in the Gulf of Finland, stands the town of Kronstadt. There, on a stone pier of the Blue Bridge, there is a special ruler with marks on it, called a footstock. For a very long time people have used it to watch how the water in the sea goes up and down. The most important mark on it is zero. From this mark we count the height of mountains, hills and cities in our whole country!
a: The height of mountains and cities
The weight of watermelons at the market

spb-n-jug-girl.s: In Tsarskoye Selo, in Catherine Park, a bronze girl sits on a rock. In her hand she holds a piece of the jug, and next to her lies a broken jug with water flowing and flowing out of it. The water comes from an underground spring, and it has been running here for more than 200 years. They say that the sculptor Pavel Sokolov invented the girl from a fable about a milkmaid who dropped her jug. And the poet Pushkin wrote poems about her.
a: From a cloud on a string

spb-n-sphinxes.s: On University Embankment, right by the Neva, lie two real Egyptian sphinxes. They are more than three thousand years old! They have the body of a lion and the face of an Egyptian king, the pharaoh Amenhotep the Third. The sphinxes were found in Egypt and brought to St Petersburg by ship in 1832. Each one weighs 23 tonnes, almost as much as four big elephants.

spb-n-shi-tsza.s: On Petrovskaya Embankment, by the steps down to the Neva, sit two unusual stone lions called shizi. They were carved from granite in China, where such lions guard entrances. In 1907 the lions were brought to St Petersburg, first by train and then by steamship. The lion holds a ball under his paw, and the lioness has put her paw on a little cub. Their manes are twisted into rings, just like curls.

spb-n-ladoga-seals.s: Close to St Petersburg lies Lake Ladoga, the biggest freshwater lake in Europe. Its water is not salty. The Neva flows out of Ladoga and runs through the whole city to the sea. And real seals live in Ladoga, the Ladoga ringed seals! There are none like them anywhere else in the world, and they are carefully protected. In summer the seals love to lie on the rocks by little islands and warm themselves in the sun.

spb-a-pavlovsk.s: In 1777 a son, Alexander, was born to Paul, who would one day be tsar. His grandmother, Empress Catherine the Great, was very happy and gave his parents a piece of land with a forest and a little river. That is how Pavlovsk began: a palace with columns and a huge park. Paths wind through it, and there are ponds, little bridges, shady avenues and small pavilions. The park was made like a real picture of a forest, so that it is nice to walk in at any time of year. In winter people go skiing here.

spb-a-ermitazh-name.s: The word “hermitage” is French. It means a “quiet, private place” where you can rest from the noise. In 1764 Empress Catherine the Great bought several hundred paintings and hung them in small rooms next to her own. She showed them only to her friends, and she called this place her hermitage. Many years passed, the rooms became very many, and today it is one of the biggest museums in the world, and the door is open to everyone.

spb-a-gatchina.s: Not far from St Petersburg, in Gatchina, stands a grey palace that looks like a fortress. Tsar Paul the First lived in it. They say there is an underground passage in this palace that leads to Silver Lake. It has survived to this day, but now it ends in a dead end and you cannot walk through it. But around the palace there is a huge park with ponds and islands where you can go boating. You can imagine you are an explorer of underground places.

spb-a-mramorny.s: On the Neva Embankment stands the Marble Palace. Building began in 1768. Marble of different colours decorated it inside and out: pink, grey, green and white. The stone was brought from many places: from the Urals, from Karelia and even from other countries. In all there are about thirty kinds of stone, and different sources give slightly different numbers. Empress Catherine the Great gave the palace to her friend, Count Orlov. Now there is a museum here.

spb-a-pradedu.s: In front of St Michael’s Castle stands a monument to Peter the Great. On its base are carved the words: “To the great-grandfather from his great-grandson.” They were thought up by Tsar Paul the First, because he really was Peter’s great-grandson. He put up the monument in 1800 to show respect to his great-grandfather. Peter was cast as a Roman hero in a crown of leaves, on a horse without stirrups. It is a very old statue, older than the castle itself.

spb-a-nikolay-kon.s: On St Isaac’s Square stands a monument to Tsar Nicholas the First on a horse. The horse is rearing up and stands only on its two back legs. The monument was unveiled in 1859. This is rare: a heavy bronze statue is held up by just two points. So that it would not fall, its makers worked out its weight exactly and made a strong base. Pigeons circle around the monument.

spb-a-lodzhii.s: In the Hermitage there is a long gallery painted with bright pictures: flowers, birds and fairy-tale patterns. It is a copy of the famous paintings by the artist Raphael in the Vatican. Catherine the Great wanted the same beauty in St Petersburg, and she sent artists to Rome. They copied the patterns, which were then put onto canvases and hung here. Now the gallery is called Raphael’s Loggias, and it is very splendid.

spb-a-zimny.s: Today the Winter Palace is green and white, like a mint sweet. But it was not always so. In its long life it has changed colour: it was sometimes ochre, terracotta red or grey. The paint was chosen by fashion and by the taste of those who decided. If you look from Palace Square, the palace seems like a huge, splendid jewellery box.

spb-b-popov.s: In St Petersburg the scientist Alexander Popov thought up a way to send signals without wires. In March 1896 he showed it at the university: in one building letters were sent, and in another, about two hundred and fifty metres away, they were received and written down. It is believed that the first words were “Heinrich Hertz”, in honour of the scientist who discovered radio waves. Today we have radio, telephones and the internet through the air, but it all began with two words.

spb-b-cirk.s: On the bank of the Fontanka stands a round building, a circus. It was built in 1877 for an Italian, Gaetano Ciniselli, and it is one of the oldest circuses in Russia. He made the ring so that horse riders, acrobats and clowns could all perform. For almost a hundred and fifty years artists have performed there, while the audience laughs and claps. When you walk past, look at the dome: inside it is always a party.

spb-b-vaganova.s: On Architect Rossi Street stands a ballet school, the Vaganova Academy of Russian Ballet. It began in 1738, when Empress Anna Ioannovna invited children to learn dancing. Today boys and girls train there every day: the barre, steps and jumps. The street itself is very even. It is two hundred and twenty metres long, and the width of the street and the height of the houses are twenty-two metres each. The architect Rossi wanted everything to be like a good dance.

spb-b-marshak.s: Samuil Marshak wrote poems for children and lived in St Petersburg when it was called Leningrad. He translated funny English songs into Russian, and the most famous is “The House That Jack Built”. In it each line pulls the next one after it, like a chain. In Leningrad Marshak gathered young children’s writers, and together they made books and magazines for kids.

spb-b-harms.s: The poet was born in St Petersburg in 1905, and on his passport he was Daniil Yuvachev. But he began to write under the funny name Kharms, also for children. He loved to make up silly poems and stories about all kinds of absurd happenings. They were printed in the children’s magazines “Yozh” (the Hedgehog) and “Chizh” (the Siskin). If you read Kharms aloud, you are sure to smile.

spb-b-repin.s: Ilya Repin studied at the Academy of Arts in St Petersburg, and later he painted famous pictures: “Barge Haulers on the Volga” and “Reply of the Zaporozhian Cossacks to the Turkish Sultan”. He settled on the shore of the Gulf of Finland in a house he called “Penaty”. Later the village nearby was named Repino, in honour of the painter. People still go there for walks along the paths by the bay.

spb-b-kruzenshtern.s: In 1803 two ships sailed out to sea from Kronstadt, near St Petersburg: the “Nadezhda”, which means “Hope”, and the “Neva”. The captain of the “Nadezhda” was Ivan Kruzenshtern. It was the first round-the-world voyage by Russian sailors. They sailed across oceans, saw islands and new lands, and came home after three years. The sailors drew maps and brought back stories of what they had seen.

spb-b-yablochkov.s: In the old days streets were lit by candles, and later by gas. Then one day in St Petersburg electric lamps lit up on Liteyny Bridge, among the first in the city. They were invented by the inventor Pavel Yablochkov, and his lamps were called “Russian light”. They gave a bright white light and seemed like a miracle to the townspeople. Today we have electricity everywhere, but back then people came to the bridge just to look at the light.

spb-b-eiler.s: Leonhard Euler came to St Petersburg from Switzerland in 1727 and worked at the Academy of Sciences. He loved numbers so much that he made up letters for them. For example, he brought in “e” and “i”, and the sign “π”, the number pi, became known all over the world thanks to him. Euler wrote so much that his books filled dozens of volumes. There were always children around him: he had many of his own.

spb-c-neva-reka.s: The Neva is a very short river: only seventy-four kilometres. But it has a great deal of water, because it flows out of Lake Ladoga, the biggest lake in Europe. The Neva carries this water to the Gulf of Finland. Right by the gulf the river splits into branches, and the city stands on islands between them. That is why there are so many bridges in St Petersburg: without them the islands would be left on their own.

spb-c-zaliv-presnyj.s: The Gulf of Finland is part of the Baltic Sea, but its water is not nearly as salty as in the ocean. And near the city, where the Neva flows into the gulf, it is almost fresh: every second the river brings a sea of water without salt. So here, in the shallows, river fish and sea fish live as neighbours. If you licked a drop from the gulf, you would hardly taste the sea at all!

spb-c-damba-zaliv.s: Across the Gulf of Finland, from shore to shore, stretches a long dam, about twenty-five kilometres. It has gates. When the wind pushes too much water into the Neva, big gates close and do not let it into the city. On ordinary days the gates are open, and water and ships pass freely. A road runs along the dam itself, and ordinary cars drive on it. The gulf is shallow here, only a few metres deep.
a: To close when the water rises

spb-c-ledyanoj-dom.s: In the winter of 1739 to 1740, a real house made of ice was built on the Neva, not far from the Admiralty. Craftsmen carved windows, columns and even furniture out of ice. In the yard stood ice trees, with ice birds sitting on them, and next to them an ice elephant. All winter long townspeople came to admire it. But in spring the warmth did its work: the house melted, and there was just the river again.

spb-c-zoopark-1865.s: The Leningrad Zoo is one of the oldest in Russia. It opened in 1865, on the first of August by the old calendar. It began modestly: Julius and Sophia Gebhardt kept a small menagerie in a little garden and showed the animals to anyone who wanted to see them. Today hundreds of kinds of animals and birds live in the zoo. And it is thought to be one of the most northern zoos in the world.

spb-c-pamyatnik-sobake.s: In the yard of the Institute of Experimental Medicine stands a bronze monument to a dog. It was unveiled in 1935. The scientist Ivan Pavlov studied how the brain and the body work, and dogs helped him with this. The monument says thank you to them: without them many discoveries would not have happened. The dog sits calmly, as if waiting for someone to say something to it.

spb-c-nos-kovaleva.s: On Voznesensky Prospect there is a remarkable plaque on the wall of a house. A nose is carved on it. It is “Major Kovalyov’s Nose”, a monument to the hero of a story by Nikolai Gogol. In the book, a nose once left its owner and went walking around St Petersburg all by itself. The monument appeared in 1995. It was thought up by Rezo Gabriadze, a Georgian artist and film director. It is a rare monument: the hero is funny, and he has no face, only a nose!

spb-c-elisej-vasilisa.s: On Malaya Sadovaya Street two bronze cats sit on the ledges of houses, or rather a tom cat and a she-cat. The cat Yelisey has settled on house number eight, and the cat Vasilisa sits opposite, on number three. They appeared in 2000, and they were made by the sculptor Vladimir Petrovichev. Passers-by often lift their heads and look for them. They say that Yelisey the cat brings good luck, but that is not certain.
a: On a bridge over the Neva

spb-d-narodovolets.s: On Vasilyevsky Island, right by the water, stands a real submarine, the “Narodovolets”. Now it is a museum. The boat is one of the first submarines built in our country. Inside it is cramped: narrow passages, pipes and levers, and tight compartments you have to squeeze into with your head bent down. You step in and at once understand how hard life was for sailors in such an iron house under the water.

spb-d-kronshtadtskiy-sobor.s: The town of Kronstadt stands on Kotlin Island in the middle of the Gulf of Finland, like a stone little ship. Its main church is the Naval Cathedral, built for sailors. Its dome is covered with aluminium and decorated with anchors and lifebuoys. The cathedral is so big that about five thousand people could fit in it, and with its cross it is almost seventy metres tall. It was consecrated in 1913.

spb-d-linii.s: On Vasilyevsky Island the streets have a special name. They are called “lines”: First, Second, Third… Peter the Great dreamed of digging canals here, like in Venice or Amsterdam, and putting the houses along the water. The canals were never dug, but the name stayed. And there is one more oddity: the two sides of one street have different numbers. On the left side, for example, it is Third Line, and on the right side opposite it is already Fourth.

spb-d-smolnyy-sobor.s: The Smolny Cathedral is white and blue, as if it were made of sky and sugar. It was designed by the architect Rastrelli, and building began in 1748, under Empress Elizabeth. Rastrelli did not see the cathedral finished: it was completed only in 1835. The word “Smolny” comes from “smola”, which means tar: long ago on this spot there was the Smolny Yard, where tar was boiled for ships.

spb-d-eliseevskiy.s: On Nevsky Prospect stands the Yeliseyev shop. It was opened at the beginning of the twentieth century by the Yeliseyev merchants, and it is built so beautifully that it looks like a palace. The windows are huge, with coloured stained glass. Under the high ceiling hang heavy bronze chandeliers. The shop is still open today, and you can buy sweets in it. Step in, and it is as if you have walked into a fairy tale about sweets.
a: A shop that looks like a palace

spb-d-vyborg.s: If you travel north-west from St Petersburg, after about a hundred and thirty kilometres you will see Vyborg. There, on a little island, stands an old castle. It was founded in 1293, which means it is more than seven hundred years old. The main tower of the castle is named after Saint Olaf. If you climb to the top, you can see the whole little town, the bay and the roofs around.

spb-d-kolesnitsa-slavy.s: You can reach Palace Square through the huge arch of the General Staff Building. Above the arch stands a chariot, and a winged goddess of victory rides in it. The chariot is pulled by six bronze horses, striding side by side like a real team. You walk along a narrow street, and suddenly the arch opens up, and behind it is a huge square with a tall column. It is a very beautiful surprise.

uae-a-burj-khalifa.s: In Dubai stands the tallest building in the world. It is called the Burj Khalifa. It has 163 floors and is about 828 metres high. If you put football pitches end to end, you would need almost eight of them to reach that length. The building is narrow and stepped: each step rises higher than the one before, and the top seems to melt into the sky. People say the architects found the shape by looking at a desert flower.

uae-a-palm-build.s: How do you build an island in the sea? In Dubai they did it like this: sand was lifted from the bottom of the bay and poured in the right place, and big rocks were laid around it so the waves could not wash the shore away. That is how the “trunk” and sixteen “fronds” appeared. Around the whole palm they built a long breakwater shaped like a crescent moon. It shields the island from big waves, like a fence from the wind.
a: To protect the island from waves

uae-a-ski-dubai.s: In summer Dubai can be hotter than forty degrees. But inside one shopping centre there is real snow! It is called Ski Dubai. It is always cold there, white snow lies on the ground, and people go skiing, snowboarding and sledging. Special machines make the snow. You can build a snowman and throw a snowball, then step outside into the heat again. A warm jacket is handed to you right at the door.

uae-a-abra.s: You can cross Dubai Creek on an abra. It is a small wooden boat with a roof against the sun. It leaves when enough passengers have climbed in, just like a bus. The trip is short, a breeze blows on your face, and the boatman stands at the wheel. It costs very little. From the water you can see old houses and new shiny towers together. Abras have sailed here for many years.

uae-a-pearl-divers.s: A long time ago, before oil was found, Dubai lived on pearls. In summer the men sailed out on big boats into the gulf to look for pearls. They dived without any air tanks, filled a basket with shells and swam up. Not every shell has a pearl, so they had to open a great many. They sold the pearls they found to merchants, who took them to different countries.

uae-b-camel-lashes.s: The camel is made for the desert, and everything about it is clever. Its eyelashes are long and in two rows, like thick little brushes, and they keep sand out of its eyes. A camel also has a third, see-through eyelid. It covers the eye, but the camel can still see the way through it. It can close its nostrils when a sandy wind blows. And its feet are wide and soft like cushions, so they do not sink into the sand. See how well a camel is made for life in the desert?
a: To keep sand out of its eyes

uae-b-falcon-passport.s: Did you know that in the Emirates falcons have their own passports? The passport has details about the bird, and the falcon wears a little ring on its leg with a number that is also in the passport. The number tells one falcon from another. With such a passport a falcon can travel by aeroplane. The bird sits with a little hood on, so it does not get worried, and behaves calmly like a real passenger. Every airline has its own rules, but the main thing is that the bird is healthy.
a: A little ring with a number

uae-b-oryx.s: The Arabian oryx is a white antelope with two long straight horns. It lives in the desert and is used to the heat: its pale coat reflects the sunlight. An oryx’s horns are so slim that from the side they look like a single horn. Maybe that is why people once made up stories about unicorns. At one time very few oryxes were left, but people took care of them, and now they live in the wild again, in nature reserves. The oryx is a much-loved animal in the UAE.
a: From the side their horns look like one horn

uae-b-dates.s: The date palm is the best-known tree of the Emirates. It grows in the heat and loves the sun. Every year heavy bunches of golden-brown fruit ripen on the palm. These are dates. There are hundreds of kinds: soft, sweet, crunchy and dark. People eat them fresh and dried, put them in sweets and offer them to guests. In the Emirates there are date festivals where people bring the most beautiful bunches. And you can eat dates, skin and all!

uae-a-miracle-garden.s: A huge garden has grown in the desert: the Miracle Garden. Millions of flowers bloom there. Flowers make up not only flower beds but also arches, hearts, little houses and big figures. The flowers are watered drop by drop to save water. The garden opens when it is not too hot outside, because in summer it would be hard for the flowers and for people. You walk along the paths, and all around is a carpet of every colour of the rainbow.

uae-a-burj-lifts.s: The lifts in the Burj Khalifa are very fast. They travel about ten metres every second, faster than any person can run. To reach the viewing deck on the 124th floor you need only about a minute. Don’t worry: the cabin glides smoothly, and your ears just feel a little blocked, as on a plane. Different floors of the building have their own lifts, and the viewing deck waits for visitors high above the city.

uae-a-dubai-fountain.s: At the foot of the Burj Khalifa lies a big lake, and the Dubai Fountain lives in it. In the evening it starts to dance to music: hundreds of jets fly up higher than many houses, sway, twirl and sparkle with coloured lights. The music is of all kinds, Arabic and songs from other countries. People gather on the waterfront, watch and clap. It is one of the biggest dancing fountains in the world.

uae-a-penguins.s: Real penguins live in the snow park Ski Dubai. There is a small colony of them. They waddle proudly, dive into cold water and slide down the snow. The penguins are not hot at all: it is kept cool for them, like at home where it is cold. You can come to meet the penguins and see them up close. Just imagine: penguins in a country with a desert all around!

uae-a-al-fahidi.s: Old Dubai looks nothing like the skyscrapers. In the Al Fahidi quarter there are narrow lanes and houses made of stone. On the roofs stand low towers called “wind catchers”. They catch the breeze and send it down into the rooms. That is how people kept their houses cool before there were air conditioners. Nearby stands Al Fahidi Fort, which is more than two hundred years old. Today it is a museum about life in old Dubai.
a: Sent cool air into the rooms

uae-a-spice-souk.s: Next to the Gold Souk is the Spice Souk. The air there smells of cinnamon, cloves and dried lime. In sacks lie red, yellow and brown heaps. The sellers pour spices into little bags. The most expensive is saffron: it is picked by hand from the middle of crocus flowers, and a single pinch needs a great many flowers. Try to guess the smell with your eyes closed!

uae-a-metro.s: In Dubai the metro runs without a driver. A computer drives the train, and nobody sits in the cab at the front. So the best seats are at the front, by the big window: you watch the train speed between the skyscrapers and feel as if you are at the wheel. The metro opened in 2009, and most of the way it runs above the ground, on high bridges. The stations have air conditioning, because it can be very hot outside.

uae-b-dunes-red.s: In the Emirates there are deserts where the sand is quite red, as if someone had crushed a brick into it. Tiny grains of iron give it that colour: they rust in the sun and paint the grains of sand. The wind pushes the sand and piles it into dunes, real sand mountains with sharp edges. By day the crest glows orange, and in the evening it turns pink. Dunes do not stay still: over many years they slowly move house, and the wind leaves wavy patterns on the sand.

uae-b-camel-chocolate.s: People in the Emirates have drunk camel milk for a very long time. It is white and a little salty. A few years ago in Dubai someone invented an unusual treat: chocolate made with camel milk. It is made into bars and sweets, and the filling has dates, nuts and spices. Sweet-lovers from all over the world buy these sweets in pretty boxes. The camels just give the milk and have no idea what yummy sweets come from it.

uae-b-flamingo-mangrove.s: In Abu Dhabi, mangroves grow in the shallow water. They are trees that stand right in the salty sea. Their roots stick up like little tubes and help the trees breathe. Little crabs and fish live in the thickets, and pink flamingos stroll nearby. They often stand on one leg and look for food in the water. Their food makes them pink: tiny shrimps and algae. Baby flamingos are born grey. The best way to enjoy the birds is from a kayak: glide up quietly and don’t scare them.

uae-b-turtles.s: Sea turtles live off the coast of the Emirates. One of them is the hawksbill. It has a sharp beak like a bird’s and a lovely shell made of plates, like roof tiles. The hawksbill eats sea sponges. In summer the mothers come out at night onto a quiet beach and lay eggs in a hole in the sand. About two months later the babies hatch and run to the water. People make sure that nobody disturbs them.
a: In a hole in the sand on a beach

spb-birth.s: More than three hundred years ago, in 1703, Tsar Peter the Great wanted to build a new city by the sea. It was a hard place to build. There was wet, muddy land, the River Neva and a cold wind. First, people built a fortress on little Hare Island. It was called the Peter and Paul Fortress. That was how Saint Petersburg began.
a: With a fortress on Hare Island

spb-names.s: At first the city was called Saint Petersburg. Then its name changed to Petrograd, and later to Leningrad. In 1991 the city got its first name back. And people love it and just call it Piter.

spb-gun.s: There is a cannon in the Peter and Paul Fortress. Every day, at twelve o'clock exactly, it goes bang! It is not for war. It tells everyone the right time. Long ago, people in the city set their watches by this bang. The cannon has no cannonball. It just makes a loud bang.

spb-rider.s: By the River Neva stands a big statue of Peter the Great. The tsar sits on a horse, and the horse is standing up on its back legs. A French artist, Étienne Falconet, made it. Under the horse lies a huge rock, called the Thunder Stone. The rock was found in a forest. It took many months to bring it to the city over land and water. The statue is made of bronze. The poet Pushkin named it the Bronze Horseman.

spb-cats.s: The Hermitage is one of the biggest museums in the world. It is in the Winter Palace, where the tsars used to live, and in the buildings next to it. And real cats live in the Hermitage! More than two hundred and fifty years ago, the first cats came here to catch mice. Today the cats still look after the rooms under the museum. They even have a holiday of their own.

spb-bridges.s: Petersburg is built on islands, so it has a lot of bridges. From spring to autumn, some bridges go up at night. The two halves of the bridge lift up. Then big ships can sail along the Neva. The most famous one is the Palace Bridge. If you are on the far side too late, you must wait until the bridge comes down again.
a: So that ships can sail through
So that the bridges can rest
So that the fish can fall asleep

spb-nights.s: At the start of summer, Petersburg has white nights. The sun hides for just a short time. At night it is as light outside as in the evening. You can read a book outside without a torch. This is because the city is far in the north. But in winter there is very little daylight.

spb-peterhof.s: Peterhof is near Petersburg, by the sea. It is the summer palace of Peter the Great. It has more than a hundred and fifty fountains. The best thing is this: the fountains in the Lower Park have no pumps. The water runs down from the high hills through pipes. Then it shoots up into the air. There are trick fountains too. You walk along a path — and splash! You get wet!
a: The water runs down from the hills by itself
The water is carried in buckets

spb-isaac.s: It took forty years to build Saint Isaac's Cathedral. The man who planned it was a Frenchman, Auguste de Montferrand. The huge dome is covered with gold. On a sunny day it shines over the city. Each big column was cut from one block of granite, a hard stone. And from the high walkway around the columns, all of Petersburg lies below you, as if in the palm of your hand.

spb-chizhik.s: By the River Fontanka, on a ledge of the stone wall near a bridge, sits a tiny statue of a little bird. It is Chizhik-Pyzhik, the siskin. It is only as big as your hand, so it is hard to see. People say: throw a coin, and if it stays next to the siskin, your wish will come true. It is very hard to hit, but everybody tries!

spb-kunst.s: Peter the Great loved everything strange and new: stones, shells, old tools and odd things from different countries. For them he made the first museum in Russia: the Kunstkamera. The word means “a room of strange things”. The Kunstkamera has a tower. Long ago people watched the stars from a room in the tower.

spb-garden.s: The Summer Garden is the oldest garden in Petersburg. Peter the Great planned it too. Stone statues stand along the paths. There is also a statue of Ivan Krylov, who wrote fables. A fable is a short story about animals. Around him are the animals from his stories: the monkey with glasses, the crow, the fox and many more. Try to find them all!

spb-faberge.s: Carl Fabergé lived in Petersburg. He made jewellery. For the tsar's family he made Easter eggs from gold and shiny jewels. Inside each egg was a surprise: a tiny carriage, a little ship or a toy bird that could move. Today the eggs are in museums, and some of them are in Petersburg.

spb-angel.s: A tall golden tower with a pointed top stands above the Peter and Paul Fortress. It is part of the cathedral. For a long time it was the tallest building in the city. At the very top stands an angel with a cross. The angel keeps the city safe. Once the angel needed mending. The roof worker Peter Telushkin climbed up the tower with only one rope and no frame to help him!

spb-hermitage.s: The Winter Palace by the River Neva was once the home of the Russian tsars. It has more than a thousand rooms. If you went into a new room every day, it would take years! Empress Catherine the Second collected paintings. She kept them in a separate building next to the palace. That place was called the Hermitage. In French the word means “a quiet place to be alone”. Today the Hermitage is one of the biggest museums in the world. The Winter Palace is now part of it.
a: A quiet place to be alone

spb-peacock-clock.s: The Hermitage has an amazing clock called “The Peacock”. It is a golden tree. A peacock and a rooster sit on its branches. At the top, in a cage, there is an owl. The clock is more than two hundred years old, but it can still move! When it is switched on, the owl turns its head. The peacock spreads its beautiful tail. The rooster crows. The clock face is hidden in a mushroom cap under the tree.

spb-alexander-column.s: The huge Alexander Column stands on Palace Square. It was cut from one single piece of granite, a hard stone. An angel with a cross stands on top. Nothing fixes the column to the ground. It stays up because it is so heavy! More than a thousand soldiers and workers lifted it up with ropes. And it has stood there for almost two hundred years!

spb-kazan-cathedral.s: The Kazan Cathedral stands on Nevsky Prospect. Its columns curve out in a half circle. They look like two big stone arms hugging the square. There are ninety-six columns! Andrey Voronikhin planned the cathedral. He was an architect, a person who plans buildings. As a boy he was a serf, which means he was not free. But people saw how clever he was, and he became famous.

spb-spas-mosaic.s: The Church of the Saviour on Spilled Blood stands on the Griboyedov Canal. It has colourful domes that look like lollipops. Inside, almost all the walls and ceilings are covered with mosaic. A mosaic is a picture made from tiny pieces of coloured glass, like a huge jigsaw puzzle. From far away it looks painted, but it is glass! Skilled workers made these pictures over many years.

spb-mariinsky.s: The Mariinsky Theatre is one of the most famous theatres in the world. It was named after Empress Maria Alexandrovna. Inside, the hall where people sit is blue and gold. A huge hanging lamp shines under the ceiling. In 1892 the ballet “The Nutcracker” was shown here for the first time. Peter Tchaikovsky wrote the music. People still dance it here every winter, before the New Year.

spb-aurora.s: A real old warship stands by the Petrogradskaya Embankment. It is the ship “Aurora”. It was built in Petersburg and put on the water in 1900. It is easy to know: it has three tall chimneys. Aurora is the name of an old goddess of the sunrise. Today the ship is a museum. You can go up on deck, look at the guns and find out how the sailors lived.

spb-nevsky.s: Nevsky Prospect is the main street of Petersburg. It starts at the Admiralty. On top of the Admiralty's tall tower there is a little golden ship that shines. The street is four and a half kilometres long. On the way it crosses the River Moyka, the Griboyedov Canal and the River Fontanka on bridges. It ends at the Alexander Nevsky Lavra. The street got its name from it.

spb-anichkov-horses.s: The Anichkov Bridge goes over the Fontanka, right on Nevsky Prospect. At its corners stand four bronze statues. Each one shows a young man taming a fiery horse. An artist called Peter Klodt made them. He loved horses very much. During the war the statues were taken down. People carefully buried them in a garden nearby to keep them safe. Afterwards the horses came back to their places.

spb-lion-griffin-bridges.s: Two narrow little bridges with animals go over the Griboyedov Canal. On the Lion Bridge, four lions sit. They hold chains in their mouths, and the bridge hangs from the chains. On the Bank Bridge sit griffins. They are animals from fairy tales, with a lion's body and wings. The griffins' wings are golden! You can only walk on these little bridges.

spb-fontanka.s: The River Fontanka flows through the middle of Petersburg. Long ago it did not even have a real name. People called it Bezymyanny Yerik, which means “a stream with no name”. Then people made the Summer Garden with its fountains nearby. The water for the fountains came from this little river. That is how the river became the Fontanka. Today people go for boat trips on it.
a: It gave water to the fountains

spb-new-holland.s: New Holland is an island shaped like a triangle. It appeared when people dug canals around it. Logs for ships were kept and dried there. It was named after Holland, where Peter the Great learned to build ships. On the Moyka side you can see a huge stone arch. Boats used to sail through it into the island. Today there is a park here. In summer everybody lies on the grass, and in winter people go ice skating.

spb-rostral-columns.s: Two red columns stand at the tip of Vasilyevsky Island. The front parts of ships stick out of them. They are called rostra, so the columns are called the Rostral Columns. Long ago a fire burned on top to show ships the way. Now the fire is lit on holidays. At the bottom sit stone giants. People say they are the rivers Volga, Dnieper, Neva and Volkhov.

spb-sphinxes.s: Two sphinxes lie by the Neva, near the Academy of Arts. A sphinx is a lion with a human head. These are real, from Ancient Egypt! They were cut from granite, a hard stone, more than three thousand years ago. Their faces look like the Egyptian king Amenhotep the Third. The sphinxes came to Petersburg by ship across the sea. Now they look at each other across the Neva.

spb-botanic-garden.s: Peter the Great started the Botanical Garden in 1714. At first people grew herbs for medicine here, so it was called the Apothecary Garden. Now palms and flowers from hot countries grow in its glass greenhouses. The most famous plant is the cactus “Queen of the Night”. Its huge white flower opens at night. By morning it fades. So that everyone can see it, the garden is sometimes open at night!

spb-elagin.s: Yelagin Island is a big green park with no cars. You can walk along the paths, go out in a boat and feed the squirrels. The island is named after one of its owners, Ivan Yelagin. At the west end of the island, on a narrow strip of land, sit stone lions. People love to watch the sun go down into the Gulf of Finland from here.

spb-kronstadt.s: Kronstadt is a city on Kotlin Island, in the middle of the Gulf of Finland. You can get there by car along a dam, a long wall in the water. You can even drive through a tunnel under the water. In Kronstadt, on a bridge, there is a copper plate with a little line on it. It is the footstock, a mark for the level of the sea. In Russia, the height of mountains and the depth of seas are measured from it. So all the measuring in Russia starts here!
a: The height of mountains and the depth of seas

spb-amber-room.s: The blue Catherine Palace stands in Tsarskoye Selo. The Amber Room is inside it. The walls are covered with amber. Amber is the hard, golden sap of trees that grew very long ago. A king of Prussia gave this room to Peter the Great many years ago. In the war it vanished, and nobody has ever found it. So skilled workers spent more than twenty years making it again. Now it shines once more, like honey in the sun.

spb-pavlovsk-squirrels.s: Pavlovsk is a small town near Petersburg. It has a huge park and a palace. The main animals living in the park are squirrels! They are not afraid of people at all. Hold out your hand with a nut on it, and keep still. A squirrel may jump down from a tree and take the nut from your hand. But the nuts must have no salt and must not be roasted. That is better for squirrels.

spb-gatchina.s: The Birch House stands in Gatchina Park. From outside it looks like a pile of firewood. But inside there are lovely rooms hidden! It was a surprise gift from his wife to Paul, who later became Emperor. And a path under the ground goes from Gatchina Palace to Silver Lake. There is a little cave there called “Echo”. Shout, and it answers you!

spb-oranienbaum.s: Oranienbaum is an old palace with a park, by the Gulf of Finland. In German, its name means “orange tree”. In the time of Catherine the Second, people built a Rolling Hill here. Guests sat in little carts and raced down a long slope. The hill is gone now, but a pretty little house is still there. And in Portugal such rides are still called “Russian mountains”!

spb-smolny.s: The blue and white Smolny Cathedral stands by the Neva. It looks like a fancy cake. Its name comes from the Russian word “smola”, which means tar. Tar is a sticky black stuff. In the time of Peter the Great there was a Tar Yard here. Tar was kept there for ships, so that they would not leak. Later the Smolny Institute opened nearby. It was one of the first schools for girls in Russia.

spb-metro.s: The Petersburg metro is one of the deepest in the world. It had to be built far down under the ground. Above it there is wet, soft ground, rivers and canals. The deepest station in Russia is “Admiralteyskaya”. It is eighty-six metres down. That is almost like a building with thirty floors, but going down! That is why the escalators here are very long.

spb-lakhta.s: A glass tower stands in Lakhta, on the shore of the Gulf of Finland. With its pointed top it is four hundred and sixty-two metres tall. It is the tallest building in Europe. The tower twists up like a flame. On a clear day you can see it from many parts of the city. Right next to it is the Gulf of Finland. In summer you can run about on the sand and watch the sunset.
a: In Lakhta, by the Gulf of Finland
On the roof of the Hermitage

spb-h-domik.s: When the city was just starting, people built a small wooden house for Tsar Peter the Great. Soldiers who were also carpenters built it in just three days! The logs were painted to look like bricks. Peter lived in it in summer and looked out of the windows at the Neva. The little house is still there today. A stone house carefully covers it from above, like a jewellery box.

spb-h-plotnik.s: Peter the Great wanted Russia to have its own navy, which means its own warships. He went to Holland. He got a job as an ordinary carpenter at a shipyard, a place where ships are built. People there called him Peter Mikhailov. With the best craftsmen he built a real ship. In Petersburg, Peter made a big shipyard, the Admiralty. He often picked up an axe himself and worked next to the shipbuilders.

spb-h-botik.s: When Peter was a young man, he found a little boat with a sail in an old barn. It was a botik, from another country. A Dutch craftsman mended the botik, and Peter learned to sail in it. That was how he began to love the sea. Many years later Peter brought the botik to Petersburg. He sailed it along the Neva himself, with big ships sailing behind. Since then people call the botik “the grandfather of Russian ships”. After all, everything began with it.

spb-h-assamblei.s: In 1718 Peter the Great thought up parties called “assemblies” in Petersburg. These were happy evenings in the houses of important people. Guests danced, talked, and played chess and draughts. Women were invited too. That had never happened in Russia before. Peter came to these evenings himself and danced with everyone.

spb-h-ekaterina.s: Empress Catherine the Second loved paintings very much. In 1764 she bought more than two hundred paintings at once from a trader from Berlin. She kept her treasures in a place called the Hermitage. It is a French word. It means “a quiet place to be alone”. At first only the empress and her guests saw the paintings. Now her collection has grown into a huge museum for everyone.

spb-h-licej.s: In 1811 a lyceum, a school for boys, opened in Tsarskoye Selo near Petersburg. One of the first pupils was twelve-year-old Sasha Pushkin. His friends called him “the Frenchman”, because he knew French very well. At a test, Pushkin read his poems to the old, famous poet Derzhavin. Derzhavin was so happy that he wanted to hug the young poet. But the boy ran away because he felt shy.

spb-h-mendeleev.s: Everything around us is made of tiny bricks called elements. Iron, gold and oxygen are elements. A scientist from Petersburg, Dmitri Mendeleev, put them in order in one table. For some he left empty squares. He said: they will be found one day! A few years later, scientists really did find these elements. A huge Mendeleev table is on the wall of a building on Moskovsky Prospect.

spb-h-pavlov.s: The scientist Ivan Pavlov studied how our bodies work, and dogs helped him. He noticed something. If the same sound always plays before food, a dog soon waits for a treat when it hears the sound. For his discoveries Pavlov was the first person in Russia to win the Nobel Prize. He was very thankful to the dogs. He asked for a statue of a dog to be put up in Petersburg.

spb-h-lomonosov.s: Mikhail Lomonosov was a scientist and a poet. He learned how to make coloured glass, called smalt. To get the colours he wanted, Lomonosov tried thousands of tests. With his helpers he made pictures from small pieces of smalt. These pictures are called mosaics. His big mosaic about Peter the Great's win at Poltava is on the stairs in the building of the Academy of Sciences in Petersburg.

spb-h-pavlova.s: Anna Pavlova was born in Petersburg. One day her mum took her to the theatre to see the ballet “The Sleeping Beauty”. Anya said later that from that day she only dreamed of dancing. She went to a ballet school and became a famous ballerina. The dance “The Swan” was made for her. She travelled all over the world with it. A light, sweet cake was even named after her: “Pavlova”.

spb-h-chajkovskij.s: Peter Tchaikovsky loved music from the time he was little. But he was sent to Petersburg to study law. He finished school and got a job as an office worker, sorting papers all day. But he could not stop thinking about music. Then the first music school in Russia opened in Petersburg. Tchaikovsky became one of its first students. He left his job and became a composer, a person who writes music. Now the whole world knows him.

spb-h-navodnenie.s: The Neva flows into the sea, the Gulf of Finland. In autumn, a strong wind from the sea sometimes pushes the water back into the river. Then the Neva spills over its banks. This is called a flood. Some houses have marks on their walls. The water once rose up to that line. The biggest flood was in 1824. Today a dam in the gulf, a big wall in the water, keeps the city safe. Its gates close when the water gets high.

spb-h-ledohod.s: All winter the Neva is covered with thick ice. In spring the ice cracks and breaks into big pieces. They float away to the sea. People call this the ice drift. Long ago, when the river was free of ice, the chief of the Peter and Paul Fortress brought the tsar a cup of Neva water. It was a sign: the river is free, and ships can sail again.

spb-h-koryushka.s: In spring, when the ice melts, a little silver fish called smelt swims into the Neva from the Gulf of Finland. It has a funny smell. It smells of fresh cucumbers! In spring smelt is sold all over the city. People fry it and eat plates and plates of it. In May, St Petersburg even has a smelt festival. For people in St Petersburg, this little fish is a sure sign of spring.

spb-h-parusa.s: Every summer St Petersburg has a party for young people who have finished school. It is called “Scarlet Sails”. Scarlet means bright red. At night a ship with scarlet sails floats along the Neva, and fireworks boom in the sky. The name comes from a book by Alexander Grin. In the book, a girl called Assol waited for a ship with scarlet sails, and her dream came true.
